Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed1de8c2db206be39aebd012e6c47503263bbf80` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a8e35fa65f1bdd3ac689587df2e778f1de00cdae` — the merge of head `ce576d209850de65974c6c0effc3091abeaff31b` into base `ed1de8c2db206be39aebd012e6c47503263bbf80`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a8e35fa65f1bdd3ac689587df2e778f1de00cdae && git checkout a8e35fa65f1bdd3ac689587df2e778f1de00cdae
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ed1de8c2db206be39aebd012e6c47503263bbf80 ce576d209850de65974c6c0effc3091abeaff31b && git checkout -B drift-repro ed1de8c2db206be39aebd012e6c47503263bbf80 && git merge --no-ff ce576d209850de65974c6c0effc3091abeaff31b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed1de8c2db206be39aebd012e6c47503263bbf80
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ed1de8c2db206be39aebd012e6c47503263bbf80` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**`Type Check · source gates` is red because of the lane-wide wall #22744, not because of this change.** `domain:spec` seat 2 (#18549) · session `session_016njDy8ozy9B9Ns5Y8kAWEK`.

- **The failing check:** `Type Check · source gates` on `ce576d2098`, at the step `render-projection-diff.ts --base HEAD^1`. It fails with `Cannot find module '../src/migrations/registry'`, thrown in the BASE tree.
- **Why it is not this PR's:** since #22706 (`ed1de8c2db`), the migration registry is generated and git-ignored, so a base archive at or after that commit lacks it. #22744 records the same failure on PRs that touch no `packages/spec` file.
- **The fix exists but is not ported here:** PR #22750, a draft by `domain:spec` seat 1, edits `render-projection-diff.ts`. Porting it would duplicate an in-flight change to the same tooling file inside a spec feature PR. This PR waits for #22750 instead. The check is re-run once #22750 lands, and the PR is then reviewed on that reading.

The gates behind that step in the same lane (`check:export-origins`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:docs`, skill refs, react-blocks) are therefore unmeasured in CI on this head; enqueue waits for #22750 to land and this check to be re-read green.
